headline: NAB's credit impairment charge (CIC) rose $105m or 14.4% to $833m in FY25 from $728m in FY24 (cash basis). The increase was driven by a higher individually assessed charge (+$328m to $964m), primarily in Corporate & Institutional Banking, partially offset by a lower collective charge (from a $92m charge to a $131m write-back, -$223m). CIC to GLAs (annualised) rose 1bp to 0.11%. The provision-type bridge (new and increased +$329m, write-backs -$46m, recoveries +$45m, collective -$223m) sums to +$105m. By division: C&IB +$153m, Corporate Functions +$83m, B&PB +$6m, NZ -$104m, Personal -$33m. The presentation corroborates the total (FY25 348+485=833; FY24 363+365=728) and the B&PB and NZ divisional charges.

drivers.columns: Sep 25 col vs Sep 24 col, New and increased row
drivers.narrative: New and increased individually assessed charge rose $329m to $1,192m (FY24 $863m), driven by an increased charge in C&IB for impairment of a small number of customers combined with non-recurrence of write-backs/recoveries in Sep 2024, plus modest increases across B&PB and NZ business lending and unsecured retail in Personal Banking. Where: C&IB +$153m (146 vs write-back 7), B&PB +$6m (529 vs 523), NZ -$104m (25 vs 129), Personal -$33m (255 vs 288).

drivers.columns: Sep 25 col vs Sep 24 col, Write-backs and Recoveries rows
drivers.narrative: Write-backs increased $46m to $178m (FY24 $132m), reducing the charge; recoveries of amounts previously written off fell $45m to $50m (FY24 $95m), increasing the charge. Net -$1m within the individually assessed total.

drivers.columns: Sep 25 col vs Sep 24 col, Collective row
drivers.narrative: Collective moved from a $92m charge to a $131m write-back (-$223m), driven by a net release of forward-looking provisions ($283m release) combined with release of provisions for customers transferred to individually assessed, partially offset by volume growth in B&PB business lending and asset quality deterioration. Where: Corporate Functions write-back fell $83m to $122m (FY24 $205m).

notable_items: CIC to GLAs annualised rose 1bp to 0.11% (FY24 0.10%)
Collective write-back includes $283m release from forward-looking provisions

disagreements.explanation: The results book divisional table (page 40) shows C&IB CIC of $146m FY25, and the divisional deltas sum exactly to the group total. The presentation's half-yearly C&IB CIC chart implies $103m, likely a different scope (e.g. NAB Asset Servicing wind-down).

limitations: The presentation's C&IB CIC chart (page 58, half-yearly values 30+73=103 for FY25) appears to differ from the results book's C&IB charge of $146m; the results book is authoritative and its divisional numbers sum exactly to the total, so the presentation figure is treated as a different scope/presentation.
The presentation page 26 CIC walk chart is a half-yearly (2H25) decomposition, not the FY25-vs-FY24 full-year comparison; it is used only to corroborate the total, not as a driver source.
The divisional deltas are the 'where' layer and are attributed to provision-type drivers per the bank's stated reasons; they are not a separate quantified bridge.

evidence_records.quote: The write-back for the September 2025 full year of $131 million was driven by a net release of forward-looking provisions, combined with the release of provisions held for customers that transferred to individually assessed during the September 2025 full year. This was partially offset by the impact of volume growth in the Business and Private Banking business lending portfolio, combined with deterioration in asset quality across the Australian lending portfolio.

Credit impairment charge was $833 million, versus a FY24 charge of $728 million. The FY25 charge includes individually assessed charges of $964 million and a $131 million release from collective provisions.
